description:
Statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl, its copybooks, its BMS mapset and the shipped ASCII fixtures. It was NOT captured from, recorded against, or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL: executing these programs is empirically impossible in this environment (no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services, and DFHAID/DFHBMSCA/DFHATTR are absent from the repository). That substitutes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else - see AAP 0.7.6 and risk R-A, where the substitution is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than silently absorbed. review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided", so no user-specified Rule governs this file; enterprise best practice governs instead and the absence is not treated as licence to lower the bar.

WHAT THIS CASE OWNS: both failing arms of paragraph 1250-EDIT-SIGNED-9V2 (:2180-2223), and the 25-character label truncation that one of its five call sites suffers. It asserts the VALIDATION outcome only; the numeric conversion these same five fields undergo belongs to the sibling cases that drive account.AccountUpdateService.

THE PARAGRAPH, IN ITS EXACT ORDER. :2181 SET FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-NOT-OK TO TRUE - pessimistic first, so every later arm overwrites rather than establishes. :2184-2185 the blank test, LOW-VALUES or SPACES, which on success sets INPUT-ERROR and FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-BLANK (:2186-2187), composes TRIM(WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME) followed by ' must be supplied.' (:2190-2191) under the IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guard at :2188, and jumps to the exit at :2196. :2201 IF FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(...) = 0 CONTINUE ELSE, whose ELSE sets INPUT-ERROR and FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-NOT-OK (:2204-2205), composes TRIM(...) followed by ' is not valid' (:2208-2209) under the same guard at :2206, and jumps to the exit at :2213. Falling through both reaches :2218 SET FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-ISVALID TO TRUE. The three outcomes are the three 88-levels on WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT PIC X(1) at :56: ISVALID is LOW-VALUES, NOT-OK is '0', BLANK is 'B'.

THE TWO TAILS DIFFER IN PUNCTUATION AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LOAD-BEARING. ' must be supplied.' at :2191 ends WITH a full stop. ' is not valid' at :2209 ends WITHOUT one. Each was copied from its own source line rather than from the other, because a reader who normalises the two has silently changed one observable byte of output.

THE 26-INTO-25 TRUNCATION, WHICH IS THIS CASE'S DISTINCT TARGET. WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME is declared PIC X(25) at :53. The five 1250 call sites and the labels they MOVE into it are :1484 'Credit Limit' (12 characters), :1496 'Cash Credit Limit' (17), :1509 'Current Balance' (15), :1515 'Current Cycle Credit Limit' (26) and :1522 'Current Cycle Debit Limit' (25). A COBOL MOVE of a 26-character literal into PIC X(25) truncates on the RIGHT, so the fourth label arrives as 'Current Cycle Credit Limi', FUNCTION TRIM returns that, and the composed message reads 'Current Cycle Credit Limi is not valid' - 38 characters, with the final 't' of 'Limit' ABSENT. The adjacent :1522 label is 25 characters and fits exactly, which is precisely why this one-character pair is worth a dedicated case. The missing letter is real, observable behaviour and is reproduced here rather than repaired; restoring it would be a behaviour change dressed up as a typo fix.

THE UNREACHABLE 88-LEVEL PAIR, ASSERTED NOWHERE. :505-506 declare 88 CRED-LIMIT-IS-BLANK VALUE 'Credit Limit must be supplied' - without a trailing full stop - and :507-508 declare 88 CRED-LIMIT-IS-NOT-VALID VALUE 'Credit Limit is not valid'. Neither condition name is SET anywhere in the program, so neither text can ever reach WS-RETURN-MSG. Two nearly identical wordings therefore exist in the source and only the composed one is observable. This case asserts the composed text and deliberately asserts neither 88-level text; they are recorded here as a documented source oddity so that a future reader does not 'correct' the composed message to match the dead literal.

FIRST-MESSAGE-WINS, AND THE ORDERING THIS CASE NEEDS. :876 sets WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at entry, and every message write inside 1250 is wrapped in IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF, so across the five sequential call sites only the EARLIEST failing one leaves a message behind. To make the truncated label observable the cycle-credit site at :1515 must be the first failure, so this case leaves Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit and Current Balance valid, and it also leaves the four sites that run before them valid - Account Status at :1472, and the Open, Expiry and Reissue dates at :1478, :1490 and :1503, each of which would otherwise claim the message first. The verified edit order in 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS is Account Status, Open Date, Credit Limit, Expiry Date, Cash Credit Limit, Reissue Date, Current Balance, Current Cycle Credit Limit, Current Cycle Debit Limit, and only then SSN, date of birth, FICO, the names, the address, state, zip, city, country, the two phone numbers, the EFT account id and the primary-card-holder flag.

BOTH ARMS IN ONE INVOCATION. ACRCYCRI carries '+      1.020.00', which has two decimal points, so TEST-NUMVAL-C returns non-zero and :1515 takes the INVALID arm - the message that survives. ACRCYDBI carries fifteen spaces, so 1100-RECEIVE-MAP at :1129-1131 moves LOW-VALUES into ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-X and :1522 takes the BLANK arm. Its ' must be supplied.' text is NEVER COMPOSED, because WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is already false by then; what remains observable is its FLAG and its attribute consequence. That distinction is the assertion, not an omission.

THE BLANK ARM'S TEXT IS NOT ASSERTABLE HERE. ParityCase models exactly one invocation - one screenRequest and one expectedResponse, whose sends list is the several SENDs of that single invocation rather than several invocations. Since first-message-wins makes exactly one composed text observable per invocation, 'Credit Limit must be supplied.' with its full stop belongs to a sibling COACTUPC case that makes the Credit Limit site at :1484 the first failing one. This case must not do that: a failure at :1484 would suppress the very truncated label case13 exists to pin. No sibling case number is asserted here, because this file cannot verify another file's contents.

THE PER-FIELD FLAG TRIPLES AT :196-215. WS-EDIT-CREDIT-LIMIT (:196), WS-EDIT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT (:200), WS-EDIT-CURR-BAL (:204), WS-EDIT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT (:208) and WS-EDIT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT (:212) each carry the same ISVALID / NOT-OK / BLANK triple, and :1488, :1501, :1513, :1520 and :1527 copy WS-FLG-SIGNED-NUMBER-EDIT into them after each PERFORM. The outcome asserted here is FLG-CRED-LIMIT-ISVALID, FLG-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT-ISVALID and FLG-CURR-BAL-ISVALID (all LOW-VALUES), FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-NOT-OK ('0') and FLG-CURR-CYC-DEBIT-BLANK ('B'). Those five verdicts are observable through the screen: ACRCYCRC and ACRCYDBC carry DFHRED, ACRCYDBO carries the '*' overlay, and the cursor lands on ACRCYCRL.

HOW CSSETATY MAKES THEM VISIBLE. app/cpy/CSSETATY.cpy - copied 39 times into 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS, with the five signed-numeric sites at :3232, :3256, :3280, :3286 and :3292 - moves DFHRED into the xxxC COLOUR item when a field is NOT-OK or BLANK and CDEMO-PGM-REENTER holds, and then, only when the field is BLANK, moves '*' into the xxxO OUTPUT item. The red goes to an attribute; the asterisk goes to the field value. Both halves are exercised here: ACRCYCRC is DFHRED with no asterisk because the field is NOT-OK, and ACRCYDBC is DFHRED with ACRCYDBO overwritten to '*' followed by fourteen spaces because the field is BLANK. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is '1', so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER holds and the guard is satisfied; on the ENTER path neither would be applied.

FOUR MORE DFHRED FIELDS, CAUSED BY THE SHIPPED FIXTURE DATA ITSELF AND PRESERVED RATHER THAN TIDIED. ACSTFCOC is DFHRED because custdata.txt row 0 carries FICO 274 while 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE at :2514 requires the 88 FICO-RANGE-IS-VALID range 300 THROUGH 850 declared at :848-849. ACSPH2AC is DFHRED because that row's second area code is 373, which does not occur anywhere in app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy and so fails the 88 VALID-GENERAL-PURP-CODE test at :2298 - the first area code, 908, is present in that copybook and passes. ACSSTTEC and ACSZIPCC are both DFHRED because 1280-EDIT-US-STATE-ZIP-CD at :2536-2547 concatenates state 'NC' with the first two zip digits '12' and the copybook lists only NC27 and NC28 for North Carolina, and only MA12 and NY12 for the 12 prefix; that paragraph sets both FLG-STATE-NOT-OK and FLG-ZIPCODE-NOT-OK together. All four failures are ordered after :1515, so first-message-wins suppresses each of their texts and none disturbs the message this case pins. They are asserted exactly as they occur.

WHY THE EDITS RUN AT ALL. 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS returns early at :1463-1467 when 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW finds nothing changed, so a case that resubmits an identical screen never reaches 1250. Here ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACUP-NEW-CURR-CYC-DEBIT both differ from their ACUP-OLD counterparts, and they do so for a precise reason: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP performs the COMPUTE into the numeric REDEFINES only when TEST-NUMVAL-C succeeds (:1120-1125 and :1134-1139), so for these two fields the twelve-byte commarea items keep the spaces they arrived with rather than the account's zoned images. The comparison at :1695-1696 therefore reports a change, :1470 sets ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, and because INPUT-ERROR is set the :1671-1675 test leaves that state standing.

WHERE THAT STATE LEADS. 2000-DECIDE-ACTION takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :2596 and CONTINUEs, so no repository operation occurs on this path - hence no write, and a final state identical to the pre-state. 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-MADE at :2718, because 'E' is one of that 88's values, so the screen is repainted by 3203-SHOW-UPDATED-VALUES from what was received rather than from the record. There each of the five monetary fields is rendered through WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2-F, declared PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 at :371, only when its flag says ISVALID, and is otherwise echoed as the raw fifteen bytes that arrived (:2874-2909). So ACRDLIMO, ACSHLIMO and ACURBALO carry the edited forms '+      2,020.00', '+      1,020.00' and '+        194.00', while ACRCYCRO carries the raw '+      1.020.00' verbatim. 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG then takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :2964, setting PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES, and :2979 and :2981 move WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) into INFOMSGO PIC X(45) and WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) - both widening moves, space-padded on the right, which is why the message is asserted at 75 characters on one channel and 78 on the other.

ONE MORE PRESERVED ODDITY: AADDGRPO. The group id is not editable on this screen and arrives as ten spaces, so :1213-1215 moves LOW-VALUES - not spaces - into ACUP-NEW-GROUP-ID, and :2921 echoes that to AADDGRPO. The field is therefore asserted as ten NUL bytes rather than ten spaces, which is a real divergence from the same field on the fetch path, where 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES copies the account record's ten spaces instead. It also means the comparison at :1697-1700 sees a difference here too.

CURSOR. 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS positions the cursor with a single ordered EVALUATE at :3009-3167 whose first matching arm wins. FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA is an 88 on WS-INFO-MSG which 3250 has already overwritten with PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES, and NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is an 88 on WS-RETURN-MSG which now holds the error text, so both leading arms are false; the account filter is valid, and the account-status, open-date, credit-limit, expiry-date, cash-credit-limit, reissue-date and current-balance arms are all valid. The first arm that matches is FLG-CURR-CYC-CREDIT-NOT-OK at :3070, so MOVE -1 reaches ACRCYCRL and that length item is the cursor. The :3074 arm for the debit field is never reached, which is itself part of the ordering assertion.

GATES. G15 and G16 - twenty declarative cases per program, seeded from the real app/data/ASCII fixtures, with the cardxref rows left RAW at their 36 shipped bytes and widened to the 50 that CVACT03Y declares by the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation rather than by a hand-padded row. G17 and G18 - the comparison is field by field and the diff count must be zero. G30 - the five call sites run in source order and the guard chain inside 1250 short-circuits on the first failing test, so both the site order and the arm order are asserted. G37 - no server-side state: the commarea, the AID and every screen value travel in the payload, including this program's own 873-byte extension. G38 - both halves, DFHRED alone for a NOT-OK field and DFHRED plus '*' for a BLANK one, each only under CDEMO-PGM-REENTER. G51 - the unit kind is CONTROLLER_POJO and account.AccountUpdateController is constructed directly, with no MockMvc and no HTTP in the path. NOT APPLICABLE, stated rather than assumed: G32, which covers CBSTM03A's backward loop-forming GO TOs and has no counterpart in COACTUPC, and G35, which covers the nine CALL 'CEE3ABD' abend sites - COACTUPC reaches none of them here, the transaction ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID at :1015, and the return code is 0.

WIDTHS, ALL TAKEN FROM PICTURE CLAUSES RATHER THAN FROM PROSE. WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME X(25) at :53; WS-EDIT-SIGNED-NUMBER-9V2-X X(15) at :55; the five ACUP-NEW-*-X alpha work items X(15) at :412-416; the five twelve-byte commarea items and their S9(10)V99 REDEFINES at :763-795; WS-RETURN-MSG X(75) at :479; WS-INFO-MSG X(40) at :463; and from app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY the five monetary screen items at X(15), INFOMSGO at X(45) and ERRMSGO at X(78). The 873-byte extension is the sum of those clauses - one byte of ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION plus 436 bytes each of ACUP-OLD-DETAILS and ACUP-NEW-DETAILS - and 160 bytes of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA bring EIBCALEN to the 1033 this case declares. The charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII and the clock is pinned, so nothing here depends on a platform default.
